Issue 1

⚠️ US Warns Gulf States of Possible Resumption of 'Short, High-Intensity' Strikes on Iran After Midterm Elections

Key summary
  • It has been reported (based on WSJ coverage) that the United States is reviewing a plan to carry out a short-term, large-scale military operation against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, and has notified several Gulf Arab states to be ready for operations. The US and Israel are said to be stepping up military preparations in case of a renewed large-scale attack on Iran.
  • The US Department of Defense reported to Congress that the cost related to the Iran war had risen to about $47.1 billion (approximately 63 trillion won) over eight months, of which about 39 trillion won was spent on ammunition replenishment alone. President Trump stated, 'I would attack Iran again if it happened again,' adding that the war 'ends when I want it to end.'
  • The Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said Iran is not attempting to restore nuclear facilities damaged by the US airstrikes. Iran criticized the West's 'attempt to justify US actions' at the UN and took a hardline stance, calling the unilateral sanctions 'economic terrorism.'

Issue 2

🚢 Strait of Hormuz Tensions: Iran Threatens Legal Action Against South Korea's Sinokor

Key summary
  • Iranian authorities announced that starting November 1, they will take legal action against South Korea's largest shipping company, Sinokor, citing violations of Strait of Hormuz transit rules. Sinokor is reported to account for about 47% of the very large crude carriers (VLCCs) passing through the Strait of Hormuz, making it the company with the 'most rule violations.' Action has reportedly already been taken against 7 of its vessels.
  • Qatar urged Iran to halt threatening actions in the Gulf region and to maintain free passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The Amir of Qatar and the President of Iran discussed the regional situation, and Qatar proposed forming a new regional security framework.
  • Iran reaffirmed its position emphasizing that it will maintain control of Hormuz (its territorial waters).

Issue 3

🛢️ Oil Price Trends: Prices Fall Below $100 After Iran's 'Conditional End to War' Remarks, Houthi Attacks a Variable

Key summary
  • International oil prices fell below $100 per barrel following remarks from the Iranian side that 'the war could end if conditions are met.' However, the possibility of further attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels has been cited as a variable that could cause a rebound in oil prices.
  • Saudi Arabia reported damage from a missile interception in Riyadh, and the Houthis claimed further attacks. Just one day after announcing the Asian Cup schedule, missiles were again fired at Saudi Arabia, continuing regional instability.
  • 'Dark fleet' tankers carrying Venezuelan crude oil were found to be moving toward the lucrative trade routes in the Gulf region bordering the Strait of Hormuz.

Issue 4

⛽ GECF Moscow Summit: Iran-Russia Energy Cooperation Strengthened

Key summary
  • Iranian President Pezeshkian attended the 8th Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) Summit held in Moscow, Russia, and stated that 'Middle East issues can be resolved by the region itself, without the United States.' In a bilateral meeting with Russian President Putin, both sides reaffirmed the expansion of cooperation and the pursuit of joint projects.
  • Iran's Acting Oil Minister Hamid Bovard discussed energy cooperation and gas swap arrangements among Iran, Russia, and Azerbaijan in Moscow, and called on GECF member states to strengthen cooperation and safeguard energy security.

Key summary

  • Eisenkot warned Netanyahu 'not to use security for political purposes.'

🕊️ Qatari Diplomacy: Proposing a New Gulf Security Framework and Regional Mediation Efforts

Key summary
  • Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs urged Iran to halt threatening actions in the Gulf region and guarantee free passage through the Strait of Hormuz, while also proposing the formation of a new regional security framework.   • The Amir of Qatar discussed overall regional affairs with the President of Iran, and Qatar also held talks with Egypt at the finance minister and central bank governor level to review economic cooperation.

This page automatically collects and summarizes public news coverage and material from relevant institutions across Qatar, Iran, other major countries and Korea. News is gathered by querying Google News RSS feeds, Naver News search, and outlet RSS (Al Jazeera, BBC, etc.) with keywords such as Qatar, the Middle East and energy; in-depth reports are collected directly from the publication boards and RSS of domestic and international research institutes, international organizations and consultancies (supplemented by news search targeting those publishers), keeping only analyses and reports on the Middle East situation, the Iran war and their industrial, supply-chain and energy repercussions. The report list accumulates items published since the war's outbreak (2026-02-28), split into domestic and overseas and ordered by publication date (newest first). Collection and summarization rely on each outlet's publicly available headline and snippet; for subscription or paywalled outlets, the full article can be opened through the provided source link only after the reader signs in or subscribes to that outlet directly. The collected articles are automatically clustered and summarized by issue, and translated into English and Arabic, by Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5) AI. The whole process runs and publishes automatically twice a day (07:00 and 15:30 Qatar time) via GitHub Actions. The Qatar government activity section separately curates only official statements, announcements and actions on the war and regional situation by Qatar government and state entities — the Emir, the Prime Minister, the ministries of Foreign Affairs, Defense and Interior, the Government Communications Office (GCO), QatarEnergy and the state news agency (QNA). Owing to automated collection some articles or reports may be missed, so please re-verify important issues against the original sources and further searches.
- Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Qatar, Commercial Section · KOTRA Doha
